observations: PATCH classification is supported by inspected post-v3.1.0 payload delta: only two already-accepted methodology wording corrections; no code/schema/key/path changes. Internal CI runner and cost-proxy qualification also need accurate changelog coverage but not new consumer migration.

All three named CLI interfaces exist with exact supplied options. release_closeout.py --mode pr checks six working-tree version anchors and creates no refs. test_public_entry.py validates existing public-entry/pin/provenance boundaries with disposable fixture copies/tags; no shared/source refs or live installation required.

Existing test_corrective_release.py resolves candidate and prior to exact commits, requires actual priorSHA, clones into a TemporaryDirectory and creates only a private fixture tag, installs core into disposable consumer, verifies commit-bound integrity/payload, and rolls back through immutable bootstrap. It prints per-command JSON and a final JSON result with core_install/rollback and inventory digests; do not invent fixed file/test counts.

HEAD-bound rehearsal must run after committed frozen source, with actual source commit and environment recorded. Its own run() propagates nonzero child commands as failure; nested expected refusals in existing public-entry tests are asserted, not laundered.

README candidate block is inside Quickstart before Local governance, so new v3.1.1 candidate pins satisfy existing public-entry checks while valid older onboarding pins remain separately labelled. Release-closeout requires current-version curl/GOVERNANCE_TAG/--tag/releasepage tokens and one roadmap candidate disposition; preserve genuine publishedv3.1.0 and installedv3.0.0 facts.

Readiness source must distinguish source preparation/acceptance from human signoff, merge, finaltag/SHA, publication and activation. Do not assert a future release SHA or make readiness self-hash into source identity.

PR145 unchanged behavioral controls may be reused after exact relevant inputs are checked. Changed anchor/readiness inputs invalidate their affected claims: normal required hosted compliance/release/fixture checks still need the new candidate; this precode approval does not satisfy merge or release gates.

No new test framework, schema, migration guide, llms regeneration or broad audit is justified. Existing release/public/rollback checks plus independent exact source review and ordinary CI provide proportionate assurance. Recce/NX and installed payload remain unchanged.

final_verdict.summary: Minimal PATCH release-preparation contract is testable with existing exact CLI checks, immutable candidate/prior identities and isolated install/rollback. Human merge/signoff/tag and activation remain separate gates.
